change: Stop replacing provisional Float endpoints after a native histogram is delivered during an eligible instant-rate probe.
proof: A histogram reaching the probe callback is nonstale and emitted in bounds; successful acquisition must be populated and have histogram allocation, so original consumption discards every tentative Float. Keep existing endpoints until that original clearing phase.
preserved: Full acquisition validation, per-skipped-Float control polling, original consuming native copies, arithmetic, diagnostics, read/progress credit, source paging and cleanup. Stale or undelivered histograms do not set the scan-local flag.
ownership: One scan-local Boolean, no persistent owner, buffer, raw-value cache, public interface or layout change. Actual eliminated copies lower work; failed-probe provisional sample peaks may decrease.

baseline_attribution.scope: Actual stage162 V1 binaries; all current runtime and Cargo inputs match. Later C fixture and documentation changes retain separate attribution.

qualification.C_scope: Float rate lifecycle controls; mixed native history covered by core units and query fixtures.

plan.compiled_policy: decision66 proportional absolute relative cumulative; no arbitrary byte veto
plan.scope: Finite native complete query times; no gain asserted before measurement.

followup.scope: No primary control exceeded the predeclared 1.05 threshold; no followup run.

limitations: Finite synthetic qualification, not universal compatibility, traffic-weighted throughput, live provider or whole-process memory.
Regular release also speeds up controls with unchanged work; its entire timing improvement is not attributed solely to discarded Float copies.
QEMU measurements establish correctness, not ARM throughput.
The 310 retained original cases keep their historical reference/source identity. The new 24 position controls are synthetic, not new Go captures.

The C wrapper initially expected 241 records instead of the current 261, including 20 direct-replay summaries; completed unit and baseline C runs were retained and reused.
Physical reads and query-memory peaks remain unchanged in the measured whole-query panel; this is reduced computation, not reduced raw I/O.
